slides.label: RAG security · Oct 8, 2026
slides.title: Your vector index can redraw your documents
slides.body: Pages inverted from stored vectors were re-identified 98.4% of the time

slides.label: The setup
slides.title: Nobody can read a vector. Right?
slides.body: Visual document retrievers store each page as about 1,000 patch vectors. Most teams treat that index as harmless.

slides.label: The attack
slides.title: Words recovered
slides.body: An inverter redraws pages from the raw index alone. It also recovers 45% of sensitive tokens.

slides.label: The match
slides.title: Pages re-identified
slides.body: Inverted pages ranked their source page first across 19,252 ViDoRe v3 pages.

slides.label: The false fix
slides.title: Shuffling doesn't hold
slides.body: A position model restores vector order and lifts re-identification from 3.8% to 93.5%.

slides.label: My take
slides.title: Protect the index like the documents
slides.body: Same access controls, same encryption, same vendor review. Token pooling is the one defence this attack hasn't broken yet.
